A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SkeletonDiffusion with the same title and authors. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete Appendices A–G support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original SkeletonDiffusion evaluations on AMASS, FreeMan, 3DPW, and Human3.6M, alongside ablations and latent-space analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains these original results and adds noisy-input, long-horizon, architectural-ablation, and computational-cost results.

M1.justification: v2 adds an inference adaptation that feeds generated motions back into predictors trained for two-second forecasts to produce five-second motions (Appendix F.4). The core architecture, covariance schedule, and losses remain unchanged; variable-length curriculum training was already documented in v1 Appendix C.

E1.justification: The four datasets and human-motion prediction task are retained. v2 extends test scenarios to synthetically corrupted 3DPW observations and five-second AMASS forecasting, adding input-noise and temporal challenges within the existing domains.

E2.justification: Zero-Velocity is added to the existing FreeMan, 3DPW, and Human3.6M comparisons (v2 Tables 2, 3, and 9); v1 included it only in the AMASS comparison. The existing learned comparators are retained.

E3.justification: v2 adds mean angle error (MAE) across the benchmark comparisons and introduces several evaluation protocols: noise of up to 2 cm on 25% of input keypoints, autoregressive five-second forecasting, and an RTX 6000 inference-cost comparison. The original dataset splits and training budgets remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 expands the component ablation with CMD and body-realism measurements, adds past-encoder fine-tuning and DCT ablations (Tables 7–8), and tests noisy zero-shot robustness, long-horizon behavior, and computational cost. The earlier covariance, normalization, convergence, PCA, and diversity-validity analyses are retained rather than newly introduced.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The additional mean and RMSE body-error measurements are evaluation metrics, not uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: v2 adds MAE scores, control rows, and results for the new ablations, noisy inputs, five-second forecasts, and computational costs. Existing main benchmark scores are retained. Small ablation values also change: between v1 Table 4 and v2 Table 7, noniso MMADE changes from 0.566 to 0.567, and Ours MMADE/MMFDE changes from 0.561/0.580 to 0.562/0.579.

T1.justification: The covariance definitions, forward/reverse diffusion derivations, training-loss mathematics, and alternative schedulers are retained, including Appendix A. Main-text equations are reorganized, while the expanded latent-space explanation restates existing assumptions.

C1.justification: Both versions retain the central claims: graph-aware nonisotropic latent diffusion improves motion realism, conventional diversity metrics can reward artifacts, and SkeletonDiffusion achieves strong benchmark performance. The additional experiments support these claims without materially redefining the contributions.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations of the DCT ablation, noisy-input and long-horizon behavior, and computational versus realism tradeoffs. It also explains why FID is restricted to Human3.6M. The fine-joint/data-scarcity limitation is retained and shortened; proposed covariance and non-Gaussian future directions are replaced by discussion of unresolved diversity evaluation.

D1.justification: v1 promises implementation details through a future code release; v2 states that the code is released and details are available (abstract and Appendix B). v2 also documents H36M model footprints and RTX 6000 timings in Table 12. Existing AMASS training and A40 timing disclosures remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds three references on manifold/protein diffusion and a BABEL reference supporting the annotation discussion, while removing Calvin Luo's diffusion overview. The principal positioning against isotropic diffusion and previous motion-prediction architectures remains intact.

P1.justification: The method exposition is substantially reorganized, including a dedicated Correlated Latent Space subsection and redistributed training explanations. Preliminaries are condensed, introduction/related-work passages are rewritten, and the appendix analysis and experiment sections are reordered with more specific cross-references.

P2.justification: Figure 3 is redrawn, benchmark tables gain MAE columns and control rows, and the main component-ablation table moves to the appendix with additional columns. Four new tables present added experiments. Existing plots and qualitative examples are retained, with several relocated or resized, including the enlarged correlation-matrix figure.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1, the added robustness tests, body-realism ablations, and computational measurements better substantiate practical claims and expose tradeoffs, while the method explanation becomes clearer. These provide a limited net improvement: the new MAE metric remains only briefly specified, and v2 introduces small unexplained discrepancies between its main and ablation tables.
